questions.q: What is the CAPM formula for an asset's expected return?
questions.explain: CAPM states expected return equals the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium (E[Rm] - Rf).

questions.q: According to CAPM, why does only systematic risk earn a return premium?
options: Because systematic risk is illegal to hedge

Because well-diversified investors have already eliminated unsystematic risk from their portfolios, so the market has no reason to compensate anyone for bearing a risk that was avoidable through diversification
Because unsystematic risk is always larger than systematic risk
Because beta only exists for bonds, not stocks
questions.explain: Since unsystematic risk can be diversified away at no cost, the market does not reward investors for bearing it. Only systematic (market) risk, measured by beta, is compensated.
Beta is the covariance between an asset's returns and the market's returns, divided by the variance of the market's returns.

questions.q: What is the key difference between the Security Market Line (SML) and the Capital Market Line (CML)?
options: They are the same line with two different names

The SML plots return against beta and holds for every correctly priced asset; the CML plots return against total risk (sigma) and holds only for efficient portfolios combining the risk-free asset and the market
The CML applies only to bonds, and the SML applies only to stocks
The SML is always flat (zero slope), while the CML always slopes upward
questions.explain: The SML is the direct graph of the CAPM equation using beta, applying to any individual asset. The CML uses total risk and applies only to efficient combinations of the risk-free asset and the market portfolio.
